title: Kepler Reach Rising
premise: Yara Winterbourne smuggles forbidden memories through the Kepler Reach, hiding recordings of Meridian Station's slow, deliberate starvation—a colony erased from every official ledger. When a distress signal arrives in Old Meridian, a language extinct for two hundred years, Yara realizes the dead colony's last survivors are still transmitting, and the corporation that erased Meridian will erase Yara next. To prove a massacre that never officially happened, Yara must ally with a customs inspector sworn to destroy them and a memory-ghost of the colony's founder living inside contraband recordings. In the end, Yara broadcasts the colony's final memories across the entire Reach, sacrificing their anonymity and nearly their life, forcing the truth into every citizen's mind at once—and choosing love and witness over the invisible safety they built their life on.
about_author: Sable Kavanagh is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the records of abandoned settlements before turning to fiction. They write about memory, erasure, and the people history prefers to forget, from a coastal town that has changed its name three times.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Opening run through Kepler Reach customs with a hold full of illegal memories, establishing the smuggling trade and Yara's careful invisibility. Beat: competent thrill masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Doesn't Exist
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A buyer requests memories of Meridian Station, which official charts say was never built. Yara realizes their own archive contains the colony's death. Beat: first crack in the safe world.

chapters.title: Inspector Voss
chapters.summary: Customs inspector Dae Voss's POV. Voss is closing in on the memory-smuggler known only as 'Winter,' unaware they share a past. Beat: duty sharpened into obsession.

chapters.title: Old Words in the Dark
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A distress signal in extinct Old Meridian arrives on a dead frequency. Yara's grandmother's lullaby matches it. Beat: dread and recognition entwined.

chapters.title: What the Starvation Sounded Like
chapters.summary: Yara plays the Meridian archive: rationing, silence, the last broadcast. The founder's recorded consciousness, Ede, half-awakens inside the data. Beat: grief as evidence.

chapters.title: The Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss is ordered off the Winter case by corporate handlers and begins to suspect why. Beat: loyalty to the service begins to sour.

chapters.title: A Buyer Named Nobody
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The mysterious Meridian buyer turns out to be a descendant of survivors, hiding in the Reach's underbelly. Beat: fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Ede Remembers Forward
chapters.summary: The memory-ghost Ede's POV. Fragmented, she recalls the massacre order and warns Yara that the corporation is still deleting witnesses. Beat: urgency from beyond death.

chapters.title: Customs House, 0300 Hours
chapters.summary: Voss nearly catches Yara mid-run; a tense standoff where neither quite lies. Beat: attraction sharpened by suspicion.

chapters.title: The Language of the Erased
chapters.summary: Yara and the survivor-descendant decode the distress signal: it's a countdown, and it's nearly finished. Beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Paper Burns Faster Than People
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss finds the falsified Meridian records and realizes the corporation authored the erasure. Beat: the loyalist's crisis of faith.

chapters.title: Winter, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Voss corners Yara; instead of an arrest, an uneasy bargain is struck over shared childhood memory. Beat: enemies become conspirators.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Yara and Voss descend to Meridian's frozen ruins to retrieve the physical black box. Beat: awe and horror in the dead colony's corridors.

chapters.title: Ede's Last Day
chapters.summary: Ede's POV. Her final recorded hours: the doors sealing, the choice to become data. Beat: sacrifice as a lesson Yara must learn.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Reach
chapters.summary: Corporate retrieval teams enter the Reach. The survivor-descendant is taken. Beat: first real loss, guilt lands on Yara.

chapters.title: The Deal Voss Refused
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Offered promotion for silence, Voss burns their career instead. Beat: duty inverted—loyalty to truth now.

chapters.title: Running the Long Dark
chapters.summary: Yara and Voss flee with the black box through unpatrolled space. Confession and closeness in the cockpit. Beat: love admitted against all prudence.

chapters.title: What Yara Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Yara's grandmother was a Meridian survivor who smuggled her out and made her promise to forget. Beat: identity reframed—Yara was always a witness.

chapters.title: The Countdown Reaches Zero
chapters.summary: The signal terminates—Meridian's last transmitter dies, or was silenced. Beat: despair; the proof may be all they have.

chapters.title: Trial by Record
chapters.summary: The pair reach an independent arbiter station; the black box is authenticated, then the arbiter is bribed. Beat: hope corrupted by institutional rot.

chapters.title: Ede, Scattered
chapters.summary: Ede's POV, degrading as corporate viruses eat the archive. She gives Yara the broadcast key before fragments go dark. Beat: a second death, mourned.

chapters.title: The Reach Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Propaganda floods the Reach painting Meridian as a plague story. Public opinion turns against 'terrorist smugglers.' Beat: isolation at its deepest.

chapters.title: Voss's Trial
chapters.summary: Voss is court-martialed in absentia; their testimony becomes the movement's first public document. Beat: defiance with a noose around it.

chapters.title: The Underbelly Rises
chapters.summary: Smugglers, dockworkers, and the forgotten colonists of other erased settlements rally to Yara. Beat: community forged from the invisible.

chapters.title: The Trap at Kepler Gate
chapters.summary: The corporation offers a prisoner exchange: the survivor-descendant for the black box. Yara knows it's a trap. Beat: love vs. duty in its cruelest form.

chapters.title: Yara's Choice
chapters.summary: Yara chooses the exchange; Voss chooses the broadcast. They split the plan between them, knowing one of them may not survive. Beat: love tested by purpose.

chapters.title: Exchange at the Gate
chapters.summary: Yara walks into the corporate station. The trap springs—but Yara has smuggled a memory of the exchange itself into the guards' own implants. Beat: the smuggler's art as weapon.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. From a hijacked relay, Voss transmits Meridian's final hours to every screen in the Reach. Beat: cathartic, terrifying climax begins.

chapters.title: The Reach Watches
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, brief and intercut: dockworkers, clerks, children watching the massacre play out. Beat: collective witness as turning point.

chapters.title: What They Did to Yara
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, in custody. Interrogation, memory-wipe threat, and Yara reciting the lullaby to hold identity together. Beat: identity as resistance.

chapters.title: The Stations Refuse
chapters.summary: Dockworkers across the Reach strike, refusing corporate shipments until Yara is released. Beat: the invisible become unignorable.

chapters.title: Voss Stands Trial, Properly
chapters.summary: Voss surrenders to testify publicly, turning the court-martial into a referendum on the erasure. Beat: courage as testimony.

chapters.title: The Second Signal
chapters.summary: A fragment of Ede, backed up in a thousand smuggled memories, surfaces in the Reach's network and corroborates everything. Beat: the dead testify.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: The arbiter station, flooded by public witness, rules the Meridian massacre proven. Corporate executives flee. Beat: justice, incomplete but real.

chapters.title: Winter, Free
chapters.summary: Yara is released into a crowd that knows their face and their name. Anonymity is gone forever. Beat: bittersweet transformation.

chapters.title: What Voss Chose
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Stripped of rank, offered reinstatement if they recant; Voss chooses the truth and Yara. Beat: love and duty reconciled at last.

chapters.title: Meridian, Remembered
chapters.summary: Yara and Voss return to the ruins to build a memorial beacon that will broadcast the colony's name forever. Beat: mourning turned to monument.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Last Cargo
chapters.summary: Yara delivers the final contraband: Meridian's memories, given freely to the descendants and the Reach's schools. Beat: the trade redeemed into gift.

chapters.title: A Name in the Registry
chapters.summary: Meridian Station is restored to the official charts. Yara adds their grandmother's name, then their own. Beat: identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Kepler Reach Rising
chapters.summary: Yara and Voss depart on a new run—not smuggling now, but carrying testimony of other erased places. Ede's fragment hums in the ship's systems, singing the lullaby. Beat: hopeful, open-ended close on witness as a way of life.
